key_insight: MedCTA shifts medical vision-language pre-training from matching single visits to learning longitudinal clinical change, so models can recognize whether abnormalities improve, stay stable, or worsen over time.
clinical_relevance: This could help AI systems interpret patient trajectories more like clinicians do, improving support for temporal tasks such as progression assessment, retrieval, and zero-shot classification.
method: Uses clinically grounded queries to build abnormality-specific visual and textual trajectories.
Models both abnormality-level change and whole-patient course progression.
Extracts structured trend supervision from longitudinal reports with an offline LLM parser, alongside static image-report alignment.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over strong medical vision-language baselines on temporal image classification, image-text retrieval, and zero-shot classification.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate trend extraction from free-text reports, so parser errors or inconsistent documentation could limit reliability.
paper_title: Clinical Trajectory Alignment for Medical Vision-Language Pre-training
